en: 9. Dhammayamaka 9.2 Pavattivāra 9.2.3.
Uppādanirodhavāra (The Chapter on Arising and Cessation)
9.2.3.1. Chapter on the Present (Paccuppannavāra) 9.2.3.1.1.
Positive Person (Anulomapuggala) In one for whom wholesome states arise, do unwholesome states cease? No.
Or, for whom unwholesome states cease, do wholesome states arise for that person? No.
For whom wholesome states arise, do indeterminate states cease for that person? No.
Or, for whom indeterminate states cease, do wholesome states arise for that person? No.
In one for whom unwholesome states arise, do indeterminate states cease? No.
Or rather, in one for whom indeterminate states cease, do unwholesome states arise? No.
9.2.3.1.2. Positive Plane (Anuloma-okāsa).
Wherever wholesome states arise, do unwholesome states cease there? Yes.
Or conversely, wherever unwholesome states cease, do wholesome states arise there? Yes.
Wherever wholesome states arise, do indeterminate states cease there? Yes.
Or, where indeterminate states cease, do wholesome states arise there?

In the case of non-percipient beings, indeterminate states cease there, but wholesome states do not arise there. In the fourfold and fivefold planes of existence, indeterminate states cease and wholesome states also arise there.
Where unwholesome states arise, do indeterminate states cease there? Yes.
Or, where indeterminate (abyākata) states cease, do unwholesome (akusala) states arise there?

In the case of non-percipient beings (asaññasatta), indeterminate states cease there, but unwholesome states do not arise there. In the fourfold and fivefold planes of existence (catuvokāra/pañcavokāra), both indeterminate states cease and unwholesome states arise there.
9.2.3.1.3. Positive Correlation: Person and Plane (Anulomapuggalokāsa)
In whomsoever wholesome states arise at a certain place, do unwholesome states cease for that person at that same place? No.
Or rather, in whomsoever unwholesome states cease at a certain place, do wholesome states arise for that person at that same place? No.
In whomsoever wholesome states arise at a certain place, do indeterminate states cease for that person at that same place? No.
Or, for whomsoever indeterminate states cease at a certain place, do wholesome states arise for that person at that place? No.
For whomsoever unwholesome states arise at a certain place, do indeterminate states cease for that person at that place? No.
Or, for whomsoever indeterminate states cease at a certain place, do unwholesome states arise for that person at that place? No.
9.2.3.1.4. Negative Person (Paccanīka-puggala) For whom wholesome states do not arise, for that person do unwholesome states not cease?
At the moment of the dissolution of unwholesome states, for those [persons] wholesome states do not arise, but it is not the case that unwholesome states do not cease for them.

They do not cease. At the moment of arising of a consciousness dissociated from the wholesome, at the moment of dissolution of a consciousness dissociated from the unwholesome, and for those who have attained cessation or are non-percipient beings, neither wholesome states nor unwholesome states arise;
and unwholesome states do not cease.
Or rather, for whom unwholesome states do not cease, for them do wholesome states not arise?
At the moment of the arising of wholesome states, unwholesome states do not cease for them, yet it is not that wholesome states do not arise for them.
[This is so] at the moment of the dissolution of a consciousness dissociated from the unwholesome and at the moment of the arising of a consciousness dissociated from the wholesome.
In those who have attained cessation and in non-percipient beings, unwholesome states do not cease and wholesome states do not arise.
Do indeterminate states not cease in one in whom wholesome states do not arise?
For all those passing away, and at the moment of the cessation of consciousness during the course of existence, wholesome states do not arise;

yet, indeterminate states do not cease for them. For all those being reborn, at the moment of the arising of consciousness dissociated from the wholesome during the course of existence, and at the moment of the cessation of wholesome and unwholesome states in the formless realm, neither wholesome nor unwholesome states arise for them.
And indeterminate states do not cease.
Or, for whomsoever indeterminate states do not cease, for them do wholesome states not arise?
At the moment of arising of wholesome states, for them indeterminate states do not cease; yet for them wholesome states [do] not [arise].
They do not arise. For all those being reborn, at the moment of the arising of a consciousness dissociated from the wholesome during the course of existence,
and for those in the formless realm at the moment of the dissolution of wholesome or unwholesome states, neither indeterminate phenomena cease nor do wholesome phenomena arise.
For whom unwholesome states do not arise, for them do indeterminate states not cease?

For all those passing away and for those during the course of existence at the moment of the cessation of consciousness, unwholesome states do not arise, but it is not that indeterminate states do not cease for them. For all those being reborn and for those during the course of existence at the moment when consciousness is dissociated from the unwholesome...
At the moment of arising of unwholesome and wholesome states in the immaterial realm, and at the moment of dissolution of those same states,
unwholesome states do not arise and indeterminate states do not cease. Or conversely,
for whomsoever indeterminate states do not cease, do unwholesome states not arise for them?
At the moment of arising of unwholesome states, indeterminate states do not cease for them,
but unwholesome states do arise for them. For all those being reborn, during the course of existence at the moment of arising of a consciousness dissociated from the unwholesome,
and at the moment of dissolution of wholesome or unwholesome states in the formless realm— for these, indeterminate states do not cease, and unwholesome states [do arise].
And [other] states do not arise.
9.2.3.1.5. Negative Spatial Analysis:
Where wholesome states do not arise, do unwholesome states not cease there? Yes.
Or, where unwholesome states do not cease, do wholesome states not arise there? Yes.
Where wholesome states do not arise, do indeterminate states not cease there? They do cease.
Or, where indeterminate states do not cease, do wholesome states not arise there? There is no such case.
Where unwholesome states do not arise, do indeterminate states not cease there? They cease.
Or else, where indeterminate states do not cease, do unwholesome states not arise there? There is none.
9.2.3.1.6. Negative Person-Space Analysis.
For whom, where wholesome states do not arise, for them there, unwholesome states do not cease?
At the moment of the dissolution of unwholesome states, for them there wholesome states do not arise, but it is not the case that for them there unwholesome states do not cease.
At the moment of the arising of a consciousness dissociated from the wholesome, [and] of a consciousness dissociated from the unwholesome...
At the moment of dissolution, for non-percipient beings, neither wholesome states arise nor do unwholesome states cease there. Or conversely:
for whomsoever unwholesome states do not cease there, do wholesome states not arise for them there?
At the moment of the arising of wholesome states, unwholesome states do not cease therein for those [beings],

but it is not that wholesome states do not arise therein for them. At the moment of the dissolution of a consciousness dissociated from the unwholesome, at the moment of the arising of a consciousness dissociated from the wholesome,
and for non-percipient beings, neither unwholesome nor wholesome states cease therein for them.
And wholesome states do not arise.
For whom, where wholesome states do not arise, for them there do those indeterminate states cease?
For all those passing away, and at the moment of the cessation of consciousness during the course of existence, for them there wholesome states do not arise.
And it is not the case that indeterminate states do not cease there for them. For all those being reborn,

at the moment of the arising of a consciousness dissociated from the wholesome during the course of existence, and at the moment of the dissolution of wholesome and unwholesome [consciousness] in the formless realm,
for them there wholesome states do not arise and indeterminate states do not cease.
Or conversely: for whom, where indeterminate (abyākata) states do not cease, for them there do not arise wholesome (kusala) states?
At the moment of the arising of wholesome states, for those [beings], indeterminate states do not cease there, yet it is not the case that wholesome states do not arise there.
For all those being reborn, and during the course of existence (pavatta) for one whose consciousness is dissociated from the wholesome...

At the moment of arising of the immaterial [states], and at the moment of dissolution of the wholesome and unwholesome [states], neither indeterminate states nor wholesome states cease there for those [beings].
For whomsoever unwholesome states do not arise in a certain place, do indeterminate states not cease for them in that same place?

For all those passing away, and at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness during the course of existence, unwholesome states do not arise therein; yet, indeterminate states do not cease therein for them.

For all those being reborn, at the moment of the arising of consciousness dissociated from the unwholesome during the course of existence, and at the moment of the dissolution of wholesome or unwholesome [consciousness] in the formless realm.
In those [states], unwholesome states do not arise and indeterminate states do not cease.
Or, conversely, for whomsoever indeterminate states do not cease in a certain place, do unwholesome states not arise for them there?
At the moment of arising of unwholesome states, indeterminate states do not cease for them there; yet it is not the case that [unwholesome states do not arise].
Therein, unwholesome states do not arise. For all those being reborn, for those during the course of existence at the moment of arising of a consciousness dissociated from the unwholesome,
and for those in the immaterial plane at the moment of dissolution of wholesome or unwholesome [consciousness],
there neither cease indeterminate states nor do unwholesome states arise therein.
9.2.3.2. The Section on the Past (Atītavāra) 9.2.3.2.1.
Positive Person (Anulomapuggala) For whom wholesome states had arisen, for that person had unwholesome states ceased? Yes.
Or, for whomsoever unwholesome states had ceased, for him had wholesome states arisen? Yes.
For whomsoever wholesome states had arisen, for him had indeterminate states ceased? Yes.
Or, for whomsoever indeterminate states had ceased, for him had wholesome states arisen? Yes.
For whom unwholesome states had arisen, for that person did indeterminate states cease? Yes.
Or rather, for whom indeterminate states ceased, for that person had unwholesome states arisen? Yes.
9.2.3.2.2. Positive Plane (Anuloma-okāsa)
Wherever wholesome states had arisen, there unwholesome states had ceased? Yes.
Or, wherever unwholesome states had ceased, there wholesome states had arisen? Yes.
Wherever wholesome states had arisen, there indeterminate states had ceased? Yes.
Or, where indeterminate states have ceased, have wholesome states arisen there?

In the case of non-percipient beings, indeterminate states have ceased there, but wholesome states have not arisen there. In the fourfold and fivefold planes of existence, both indeterminate states have ceased and wholesome states have arisen there.
Where unwholesome states have arisen, have indeterminate states ceased there? Yes.
Or, where indeterminate states have ceased, there have unwholesome states arisen?
In the case of non-percipient beings, indeterminate states have ceased there, but unwholesome states have not arisen there.
In the fourfold and fivefold planes of existence, both indeterminate states have ceased and unwholesome states have arisen there.
9.2.3.2.3. Positive Person-Space (Anuloma-Puggalokāsa) In whomsoever wholesome states had arisen in a certain place, had unwholesome states ceased in that same person in that same place? Yes.
Or conversely, in whomsoever unwholesome states had ceased in a certain place, had wholesome states arisen in that same person in that same place?
When a second unwholesome consciousness is occurring in the Pure Abodes, unwholesome states have ceased there for them,
but wholesome states have not arisen there for them. For others— those of the four-aggregate and five-aggregate planes—
both unwholesome states have ceased there and wholesome states have arisen there.
For whomsoever wholesome states had arisen at a certain place, for that person at that place, did indeterminate states cease? Yes.
Or rather, for whomsoever indeterminate states ceased at a certain place, for that person at that place, had wholesome states arisen?

[They had not]—in the case of those in the second moment of consciousness in the Pure Abodes (Suddhāvāsa), and in the case of non-percipient beings; for them, at that place, indeterminate states [ceased].
[For those beings] where indeterminate states ceased, wholesome states did not arise for them there.
For others—those of the four-constituent and five-constituent realms—both indeterminate states ceased and wholesome states arose there.
For whomsoever unwholesome states arose at a certain place, did indeterminate states cease for them at that same place? Yes.
Or conversely: for whomsoever indeterminate states had ceased at a certain place, had unwholesome states arisen for them there?

For those in the second consciousness of the Pure Abodes (suddhāvāsa) and for non-percipient beings (asaññasatta), indeterminate states had ceased there, but unwholesome states had not arisen for them there. For others belonging to the four-aggregate plane...
For those belonging to the five-aggregate plane, indeterminate states had ceased there and unwholesome states had arisen.
9.2.3.2.4. Negative Person (Paccanīka-puggala) For whom wholesome states did not arise, for that person did unwholesome states not cease? None.
Or, for whom unwholesome states had not ceased, had wholesome states not arisen for them? None.
For whom wholesome states had not arisen, had indeterminate states not ceased for them? None.
Or, for whom indeterminate states had not ceased, had wholesome states not arisen for them? None.
For whom unwholesome states did not arise, for them did indeterminate states not cease? None.
Or else, for whom indeterminate states did not cease, for them did unwholesome states not arise? None.
9.2.3.2.5. Negative Plane (Paccanīka-okāsa).
Wherever wholesome states did not arise, there unwholesome states did not cease? Yes.
Or, wherever unwholesome states did not cease, there wholesome states did not arise? Yes.
Wherever wholesome states did not arise, there indeterminate states did not cease? They did cease.
Or, where indeterminate states have not ceased, have wholesome states not arisen there? No.
Where unwholesome states have not arisen, have indeterminate states not ceased there? They have ceased.
Or, where indeterminate states have not ceased, have unwholesome states not arisen there? No.

9.2.3.2.6. Negative Person-Space (Paccanīka-Puggalokāsa) In whom, and in what [mental] state, wholesome states (*kusala-dhamma*) have not arisen, in that person and in that state, do unwholesome states (*akusala-dhamma*) not cease?
In the case of those in the Pure Abodes (*suddhāvāsa*), while a second unwholesome consciousness is occurring, in them and in that [consciousness], wholesome states have not arisen.

And yet, unwholesome states had not ceased there for them. When the second consciousness of the Pure Abodes (Suddhāvāsa) was occurring, and for non-percipient beings (asaññasatta), neither wholesome states nor unwholesome states had arisen or ceased there respectively. Or rather:
for whomsoever unwholesome states had not ceased in a certain place, had wholesome states not arisen for them in that same place? Yes, they had.
For whomsoever wholesome states had not arisen at a certain place, had indeterminate states not ceased for them there?

For those in the second moment of consciousness of the Pure Abodes (suddhāvāsa) and for non-percipient beings (asaññasatta), wholesome states had not arisen there, but it is not the case that indeterminate states had not ceased for them there. [This is so] for those being reborn in the Pure Abodes.
For those [persons], in that [place], wholesome states had not arisen and indeterminate states had not ceased.
Or, for whomsoever, in whatever place, indeterminate states had not ceased, for that person, in that place, had wholesome states not arisen? Yes.
For whomsoever, in whatever place, unwholesome states had not arisen, for that person, in that place, had indeterminate states not ceased?
When the second consciousness of the Suddhāvāsa deities is occurring, for those non-percipient beings,

unwholesome states have not arisen there, but indeterminate states have not ceased there either. For those being reborn in the Suddhāvāsa realm, neither unwholesome states nor indeterminate states have ceased there.
Or conversely, for whomsoever indeterminate states have not ceased at a certain place, have unwholesome states not arisen for them there? Yes.
9.2.3.3. Future Chapter 9.2.3.3.1.
Positive Person-Perspective.
For whom wholesome states will arise, for them unwholesome states will cease?
For those who will attain the supreme path immediately after this consciousness, wholesome states will arise, but unwholesome states will not cease for them.
For others, both wholesome states will arise [and unwholesome states will cease].
Unwholesome states will cease.
Or, for whomsoever unwholesome states will cease, will wholesome states arise for them? Yes.
For whomsoever wholesome states will arise, will indeterminate states cease for them? Yes.
Or, for whomsoever indeterminate states (abyākata-dhamma) will cease, will wholesome states (kusala-dhamma) arise for them?
For those possessing the supreme path (aggamagga-samaṅgin) and for Arahants, indeterminate states will cease, but wholesome states will not arise for them.
For others, both indeterminate states will cease and wholesome states [will arise].
And unwholesome states will arise.
For whom unwholesome states will arise, for that person will indeterminate states cease? Yes.
Or rather, for whom indeterminate states will cease, for that person will unwholesome states arise?
For those possessing the highest path (aggamaggasamaṅgī), for Arahants, and for those whose consciousness immediately following which they will attain the highest path,
indeterminate (abyākata) phenomena will cease, but unwholesome (akusala) phenomena will not arise for them.
For others, both indeterminate phenomena will cease and unwholesome phenomena will arise.
9.2.3.3.2. Positive Section (Anuloma-okāsa):
Where wholesome states will arise, will unwholesome states cease there? Yes.
Or, where unwholesome states will cease, will wholesome states arise there? Yes.
Wherever wholesome states will arise, will indeterminate states cease there? Yes.
Or else, wherever indeterminate states will cease, will wholesome states arise there?
In the case of non-percipient beings, indeterminate states will cease there, but wholesome states will not arise there.
In the fourfold plane and the fivefold plane, there are places where indeterminate states will cease and wholesome states will arise.
Is it the case that wherever unwholesome states will arise, there indeterminate states will cease? Yes.
Or conversely, is it the case that wherever indeterminate states will cease, there unwholesome states will arise?
In the realm of non-percipient beings (*asaññasatta*), indeterminate (*abyākata*) phenomena will cease there, but unwholesome (*akusala*) phenomena will not arise there.
In the fourfold and fivefold planes of existence (*vokāra*), indeterminate phenomena will cease there and unwholesome phenomena will also arise there.
9.2.3.3.3. Positive Correlation: Person and Plane (*Anulomapuggalokāsa*).
For whom, and where, will wholesome states arise, and for them, and there, will unwholesome states cease?
For those who will attain the supreme path immediately after that consciousness, wholesome states will arise there, but unwholesome states will not cease there for them.
For others—those of the four-aggregate and five-aggregate realms—[both will occur].
In those [persons], wholesome states will arise there and unwholesome states will cease there.
Or rather, for whomsoever unwholesome states will cease in a certain place, will wholesome states arise for that person in that same place? Yes.
For whomsoever wholesome states will arise in a certain place, will indeterminate states cease for that person in that same place? Yes.
Or conversely, for whomsoever indeterminate states will cease at a certain place, will wholesome states arise for them there?
For those possessing the supreme path, for Arahants, and for non-percipient beings, indeterminate states will cease there, but wholesome states will not arise for them there.
For others—those of the fourfold and fivefold aggregates—[both will occur].
In those [beings], indeterminate states will cease there and wholesome states will arise there.
For whomsoever unwholesome states will arise there, for that person will indeterminate states cease there? Yes.
Or conversely, for whomsoever indeterminate states will cease there, for that person will unwholesome states arise there?
For those possessing the highest path (aggamaggasamaṅgī), for Arahants, and for those whose consciousness immediately precedes the attainment of the highest path,
and for non-percipient beings (asaññasatta)— in these cases, indeterminate (abyākata) phenomena will cease there, but unwholesome (akusala) phenomena will not arise there for them. For others—
those belonging to the four-constituent (catuvokāra) and five-constituent (pañcavokāra) realms— in those cases, indeterminate...
...and unwholesome states will cease.
9.2.3.3.4. Negative Person (Paccanīka-puggala):
For whom wholesome states will not arise, for that person will unwholesome states not cease? Yes, they will.
Or alternatively: For whom unwholesome states will not cease, for them wholesome states will not arise?

For those who will attain the supreme path immediately after this consciousness, unwholesome states will not cease, but it is not the case that wholesome states will not arise for them. For those possessing the supreme path and for Arahants...
Unwholesome states will not cease, and wholesome states will not arise.
For one in whom wholesome states will not arise, will indeterminate states not cease?
For those possessing the highest path (the Arahants), wholesome states will not arise; yet for them, it is not the case that [indeterminate states do not cease].
Indeterminate states will not cease. At the moment of dissolution of the final consciousness, for those [beings], both wholesome states will not arise and indeterminate states will not cease.
Or rather, for whomsoever indeterminate states will not cease, will wholesome states not arise for them? Yes.
For whom unwholesome states will not arise, for them indeterminate states will not cease?
For those possessing the highest path (aggamagga), for Arahants, and for those whose consciousness immediately following which they will attain the highest path—
unwholesome states will not arise for them, but it is not the case that indeterminate states will not cease for them.
At the moment of the dissolution of the final consciousness, unwholesome states will not arise for them, and indeterminate states will not cease.
Or rather, for whomsoever indeterminate states will not cease, will unwholesome states not arise for them? Yes.
9.2.3.3.5. Negative Plane (Paccanīka-okāsa) Where wholesome states will not arise, will unwholesome states not cease there? Yes.
Or else, where unwholesome states will not cease, will wholesome states not arise there? Yes.
Where wholesome states will not arise, will indeterminate states not cease there? They will cease.
Or else, where indeterminate states will not cease, will wholesome states not arise there? There is none.
Where unwholesome states will not arise, will indeterminate states not cease there? They will cease.
Or, where indeterminate states will not cease, will unwholesome states not arise there? There is no such case.
9.2.3.3.6. Negative Person-Space:
For whomsoever, wherever wholesome states will not arise, for that person there unwholesome states will not cease? Yes.
Or rather, for whomsoever unwholesome states will not cease at a certain place, will wholesome states not arise for them there?

For those who will attain the supreme path immediately after that consciousness, unwholesome states will not cease there, yet it is not the case that wholesome states will not arise for them there. [This is so] for those possessing the supreme path.
In Arahants and in non-percipient beings, neither unwholesome states nor wholesome states will cease there.
For one in whom wholesome states will not arise at a certain place, will indeterminate states not cease there?
For those possessing the highest path (agga-magga-samaṅgī), for Arahants, and for non-percipient beings (asañña-satta), wholesome states (kusala-dhamma) will not arise there;

yet it is not the case that indeterminate states (abyākata-dhamma) will not cease there for them. At the moment of the dissolution of the final consciousness (pacchima-citta), for them, neither wholesome states nor indeterminate states will cease there.
Or rather: For whomsoever, wherever, indeterminate states will not cease, for that person there wholesome states will not arise? Yes.
For whomsoever, wherever, unwholesome states will not arise, for that person there indeterminate states will not cease?
[They will not cease] for those possessing the supreme path (aggamaggasamaṅgī), for Arahants, and for one whose consciousness immediately follows which they will attain the supreme path.
For non-percipient beings, unwholesome states will not arise there, but indeterminate states will not cease there either.
At the moment of the dissolution of the final consciousness, for them, neither unwholesome states nor indeterminate states will cease there.
Or alternatively: For whomsoever, wherever, indeterminate states will not cease, for that person, there, unwholesome states will not arise?
Yes. 9.2.3.4. Chapter on the Present and the Past. 9.2.3.4.1.
Positive Person.
For whom wholesome states arise, for that person unwholesome states have ceased? Yes.
Or conversely, for whom unwholesome states have ceased, for that person do wholesome states arise?
[They do not] in all cases at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, at the moment of the arising of consciousness dissociated from the wholesome, and for those who have attained cessation.
In non-percipient beings, unwholesome states have ceased, but wholesome states do not arise in them.
At the moment of the arising of wholesome states, both unwholesome states have ceased and wholesome states arise.
For one in whom wholesome states arise, have indeterminate states ceased? Yes.
Or, for whomsoever indeterminate states have ceased, do wholesome states arise for them?
For all beings at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, for those at the moment of the arising of a consciousness dissociated from the wholesome,
and for those who have attained cessation or are non-percipient beings— indeterminate states have ceased for them, but wholesome states do not arise for them.
At the moment of the arising of wholesome states, indeterminate states have ceased for them, and wholesome states arise.
For whomsoever unwholesome states arise, for that person have indeterminate states ceased? Yes.
Or rather, for whomsoever indeterminate states have ceased, for that person do unwholesome states arise? Yes.
At the moment of dissolution of all consciousness, at the moment of arising of consciousness dissociated from the unwholesome,
and for those who have attained cessation or are non-percipient beings, indeterminate states have ceased, but unwholesome states do not arise for them.
At the moment of arising of unwholesome states, both indeterminate states and unwholesome states have ceased and arise for them respectively.
9.2.3.4.2. Positive Plane (Anuloma-okāsa):
Where wholesome states arise, had unwholesome states ceased there?
…pe… 9.2.3.4.3. Positive Person-Plane (Anuloma-puggalokāsa)
In whomsoever wholesome states arise at a particular place, do unwholesome states cease for that person at that same place? Yes.
Or conversely, in whomsoever unwholesome states have ceased at a particular place, do wholesome states arise for that person at that same place? [No;

for all [beings] at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, and for those with a consciousness dissociated from the wholesome at the moment of its arising, [wholesome states do not arise] at that place.
Unwholesome states have ceased, but wholesome states do not arise for them there.
At the moment of the arising of wholesome states, both unwholesome states have ceased and wholesome states arise for them there.
For whomsoever wholesome states arise in a certain place, have indeterminate states ceased for them in that same place? Yes.
Or conversely, for whomsoever indeterminate states have ceased at a certain place, do wholesome states arise for them there?
For all [beings] at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, for those at the moment of the arising of a consciousness dissociated from the wholesome,
and for non-percipient beings— at these, indeterminate states have ceased, but wholesome states do not arise for them there.
At the moment of the arising of wholesome states, indeterminate states have ceased and wholesome states arise therein for those [persons].
For whomsoever unwholesome states arise therein, have indeterminate states ceased therein for them? Yes.
Or rather, for whomsoever indeterminate states have ceased therein, do unwholesome states arise therein for them?
In all [beings] at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, in those with unwholesome dissociated consciousness at the moment of its arising,
and in non-percipient beings— unwholesome states have ceased there, but unwholesome states do not arise there for them.
At the moment of the arising of unwholesome states, both indeterminate states and unwholesome states have ceased and arise there for them.
9.2.3.4.4. Negative Person (Paccanīka-puggala) For whom wholesome states do not arise, for that person have unwholesome states not ceased? They have ceased.
Or conversely, for whom unwholesome states have not ceased, for that person do wholesome states not arise? There is no such case.
For whom wholesome states do not arise, for that person have indeterminate states not ceased? They have ceased.
Or conversely, for whom indeterminate states have not ceased, for that person do wholesome states not arise? There is none.
For whom unwholesome states do not arise, for that person have indeterminate states not ceased? They have ceased.
Or, for whom indeterminate states (*abyākata-dhammā*) have not ceased, do unwholesome states (*akusala-dhammā*) not arise for them? None.
9.2.3.4.5. Negative Plane (Paccanīka-okāsa):
Where wholesome states (*kusala-dhammā*) do not arise, have unwholesome states not ceased there? …pe… (etc.)
9.2.3.4.6. Negative Person and Plane (Paccanīka-puggalokāsa) In whom, and in what plane, wholesome states do not arise;
in that same person and in that same plane, do unwholesome states not cease? [They do not.

For all persons at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, and for those at the moment of the arising of a consciousness dissociated from the wholesome—in them, in that plane, [unwholesome states do not cease].
Wholesome states do not arise, yet unwholesome states have not ceased for them there.
When the second consciousness of the Pure Abodes is occurring, and for non-percipient beings, neither wholesome nor unwholesome states have arisen or ceased respectively for them there.
Or again, for whomsoever unwholesome states had not ceased at a certain place, do wholesome states not arise for him there? Yes.
For whomsoever wholesome states do not arise at a certain place, have indeterminate states not ceased for him there?

[They have] for all beings at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, for those whose consciousness is dissociated from the wholesome at the moment of its arising, and for non-percipient beings.
For them, wholesome states do not arise there, but indeterminate states have not ceased there.
For those being reborn in the Pure Abodes, neither wholesome states nor indeterminate states have ceased there.
Or again, for whomsoever indeterminate states have not ceased at a certain place, do wholesome states not arise for them there? Yes.
For whomsoever unwholesome states do not arise at a certain place, have indeterminate states not ceased for them there?

[They have] for all [beings] at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, for those at the moment of the arising of consciousness dissociated from the unwholesome, and for non-percipient beings.
For them, unwholesome states do not arise there, but indeterminate states have not ceased there.
For those being reborn in the Pure Abodes, neither unwholesome states nor indeterminate states have ceased there.
Or conversely, for whomsoever indeterminate states have not ceased at a certain place, do unwholesome states not arise for them there? Yes.
9.2.3.5. Chapter on the Present and Future. 9.2.3.5.1.
Positive Person.
For whom wholesome states arise, for them unwholesome states will cease?
At the moment of the arising of the supreme path (aggamagga), and at the moment of the arising of that consciousness immediately after which they will attain the supreme path—
for those [beings], wholesome states arise, but unwholesome states do not [cease].
They will cease. At the moment of arising of other wholesome states, for those [beings], wholesome states arise and unwholesome states will cease.
Or rather, for whomsoever unwholesome states will cease, for that person do wholesome states arise?
For all [beings] at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, for those at the moment of the arising of a consciousness dissociated from the wholesome,
and for those who have attained cessation or are non-percipient beings, unwholesome states will cease, but wholesome states do not arise for them.
At the moment of the arising of wholesome states, both unwholesome states will cease and wholesome states arise for them.
For whom wholesome states arise, for them indeterminate states will cease? Yes.
Or rather, for whom indeterminate states will cease, for them do wholesome states arise?

[This is not the case] for all at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, for those with consciousness dissociated from the wholesome at the moment of its arising, and for those who have attained cessation.
In the case of non-percipient beings, indeterminate states will cease, but wholesome states do not arise for them.
At the moment of the arising of wholesome states, both indeterminate states will cease and wholesome states arise.
For one in whom unwholesome states arise, will indeterminate states cease? Yes.
Or, for whomsoever indeterminate states (abyākata-dhamma) will cease, do unwholesome states (akusala-dhamma) arise in them?
In all those at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, in those at the moment of the arising of a consciousness dissociated from the unwholesome,
and in those who have attained cessation or are non-percipient beings— indeterminate states will cease for them, but unwholesome states do not arise for them.
At the moment of arising of unwholesome states, indeterminate states will cease and unwholesome states arise for those [beings].
9.2.3.5.2. Positive Plane (Anuloma-okāsa):
Where wholesome states arise, will unwholesome states cease there? …pe….
9.2.3.5.3. Positive Person-Space (Anuloma-puggalokāsa) In whom, and in what place, wholesome states arise;
will unwholesome states cease in that same person, in that same place?
At the moment of the arising of the supreme path (aggamagga), and for that consciousness immediately after which one will attain the supreme path—in such a person [unwholesome states will cease].
At the moment of arising of consciousness, wholesome states arise for them there,
but unwholesome states will not cease for them there. At the moment of arising of other wholesome states, both wholesome states arise and unwholesome states will cease for them there.
Or conversely, for whomsoever unwholesome states will cease at a certain place, do wholesome states arise for them at that same place?

For all [beings] at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, and for those at the moment of the arising of a consciousness dissociated from the wholesome, unwholesome states will cease there, but wholesome states do not arise for them there. Of the wholesome...
At the moment of arising, unwholesome states will cease and wholesome states arise therein for those [beings].
For whomsoever wholesome states arise therein, will indeterminate states cease therein for that same person? Yes.
Or rather, for whomsoever indeterminate states will cease therein, do wholesome states arise therein for that same person?
In all [beings] at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, in those at the moment of the arising of a consciousness dissociated from the wholesome,
and in non-percipient beings— unwholesome-resultant indeterminate states will cease there, but wholesome states do not arise there for them.
At the moment of the arising of wholesome states, both indeterminate states and wholesome states will cease and arise there for them.
For whom, where unwholesome states arise, will indeterminate states cease there? Yes.
Or rather, for whom, where indeterminate states will cease, do unwholesome states arise there?
For all [beings] at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, at the moment of the arising of consciousness dissociated from the unwholesome, and for non-percipient beings.
For them, indeterminate states will cease there, but unwholesome states do not arise there for them.
At the moment of arising of unwholesome states, for them both indeterminate states will cease there and unwholesome states arise there.
9.2.3.5.4. Negative Person (Paccanīka-puggala)
For whom wholesome states do not arise, for them unwholesome states will not cease?
For all [beings] at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, for those at the moment of the arising of a consciousness dissociated from the wholesome,
and for those who have attained cessation or are non-percipient beings— wholesome states do not arise for them, yet it is not the case that unwholesome states will not cease for them.
At the moment of the cessation of the supreme path (aggamagga), and at the moment of the cessation of that consciousness immediately after which Arahants will attain the supreme path—
do wholesome states not arise for them, and do unwholesome states not cease? Or conversely,
for whomsoever unwholesome states do not cease, do wholesome states not arise for them?
At the moment of the arising of the supreme path (aggamagga), and at the moment of the arising of that consciousness immediately after which those who will attain the supreme path [will do so],
unwholesome states (akusala-dhamma) will not cease, but wholesome states (kusala-dhamma) do not fail to arise for them.
At the moment of the dissolution of the supreme path, and for Arahants— at the moment of the arising of that consciousness immediately after which...
At the moment of the cessation of that consciousness which will attain the highest path (aggamagga),
neither unwholesome states nor wholesome states will arise.
For one in whom wholesome states do not arise, will indeterminate states not cease?

In all [beings] at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, in those at the moment of the arising of a consciousness dissociated from the wholesome, in those who have attained cessation, and in those non-percipient beings, wholesome states do not arise; yet it is not the case that indeterminate states will not cease for them.
At the moment of the dissolution of the final consciousness, for them both wholesome states do not arise...
And indeterminate states will not cease.
Or, for whomsoever indeterminate states will not cease, do wholesome states not arise for them? Yes.
For whomsoever unwholesome states do not arise, will indeterminate states not cease for them?

In all [beings] at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, in those at the moment of the arising of a consciousness dissociated from the unwholesome, in those who have attained cessation, and in non-percipient beings, unwholesome states do not arise; yet it is not the case that indeterminate states will not cease for them.
At the moment of the dissolution of the final consciousness, for them both unwholesome states do not arise...
And indeterminate states will not cease.
Or, for whomsoever indeterminate states will not cease, do unwholesome states not arise for them? Yes.
9.2.3.5.5. Negative Plane (Paccanīka-okāsa).
Where wholesome states do not arise, will unwholesome states not cease there? … [as before] … 9.2.3.5.6.
Negative Person-Space:
For whom, where wholesome states do not arise, for that person will unwholesome states not cease there?

In all [beings] at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, and at the moment of the arising of a consciousness dissociated from the wholesome, wholesome states do not arise therein; yet it is not the case that unwholesome states will not cease therein for them.
[This is also true] at the moment of the dissolution of the supreme path (aggamagga), and for Arahants, and for one whose consciousness immediately follows which they will attain the supreme path.
At the moment of the dissolution of that consciousness, for those non-percipient beings, neither wholesome states arise nor do unwholesome states cease there. Or conversely:
for whomsoever unwholesome states will not cease there, do wholesome states not arise for them there?

At the moment of the arising of the supreme path (aggamagga), and at the moment of the arising of that consciousness immediately after which they will attain the supreme path, unwholesome states (akusala-dhamma) will not cease therein;

yet wholesome states (kusala-dhamma) do not fail to arise therein for them. At the moment of the dissolution of the supreme path, and for Arahants—at the moment of the arising of that consciousness...
At the moment of the dissolution of that consciousness of one who will attain the highest path immediately thereafter, and for non-percipient beings,
unwholesome states do not cease and wholesome states do not arise there.
For whomsoever wholesome states do not arise in a certain place, do indeterminate states not cease for them in that same place?

In all [beings] at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, in those at the moment of the arising of a consciousness dissociated from the wholesome, and in non-percipient beings—wholesome states do not arise there for them;
yet it is not the case that indeterminate states will not cease there for them.
At the moment of the dissolution of the final consciousness, for them there, wholesome states do not arise, and indeterminate [states also do not arise].
And will indeterminate states not cease for him?
Or conversely, for whomsoever indeterminate states will not cease at a certain place, do wholesome states not arise for him there? Yes.
For whomsoever unwholesome states do not arise at a certain place, will indeterminate states not cease for him there?

In all [beings] at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, in those at the moment of the arising of a consciousness dissociated from unwholesome states, and in non-percipient beings—unwholesome states do not arise therein; yet it is not that indeterminate states will not cease therein for them.
At the moment of the dissolution of the final consciousness, unwholesome states do not arise therein for them.
And indeterminate states will not cease.
Or rather, for whomsoever and wherever indeterminate states will not cease, do unwholesome states not arise for that person there? Yes.
9.2.3.6. Section on the Past and Future.
9.2.3.6.1. Positive Person (Anulomapuggala) For whom wholesome states have arisen, will unwholesome states cease for them?
For those possessing the supreme path (aggamaggasamaṅgī), for Arahants, and for those whose consciousness immediately precedes the attainment of the supreme path.
For those [beings], wholesome states have arisen, but unwholesome states will not cease for them.
For others, both wholesome states have arisen and unwholesome states will cease.
Or, for whomsoever unwholesome states will cease, have wholesome states arisen for them? Yes.
For whom wholesome states have arisen, will indeterminate states cease for them?
At the moment of the dissolution of the final consciousness, wholesome states have arisen for them, but indeterminate states will not cease for them.
For others, both wholesome states have arisen and indeterminate states will cease.
Or, for whomsoever indeterminate states (abyākatā dhammā) will cease, for that person have wholesome states (kusalā dhammā) arisen? Yes.
For whomsoever unwholesome states (akusalā dhammā) have arisen, for that person will indeterminate states cease?
At the moment of dissolution (bhaṅgakkhaṇa) of the final consciousness (pacchimacitta), unwholesome states have arisen for them, but indeterminate states will not [cease] for them.
Unwholesome states will cease. For others, unwholesome states have arisen and indeterminate states will cease.
Or else, for whomsoever indeterminate states will cease, have unwholesome states arisen for them? Yes.
9.2.3.6.2. Positive Plane (Anuloma-okāsa)
Wherever wholesome states have arisen, will unwholesome states cease there?
… [as before] … 9.2.3.6.3. Positive Person-Space:
In whomsoever wholesome states have arisen in a certain place, will unwholesome states cease in that person in that same place?
For those possessing the highest path (aggamaggasamaṅgī), for Arahants, and for those whose consciousness immediately following [this] will attain the highest path—
wholesome states (kusalā dhammā) have arisen in them therein, but unwholesome states (akusalā dhammā) will not cease in them therein.
For others, namely those of the four-aggregate and five-aggregate realms, wholesome states have arisen in them therein, and unwholesome states [have also arisen].
And will unwholesome states cease? Or, conversely, in whomsoever unwholesome states will cease at a certain place, have wholesome states arisen in them there?
[Answer: In the case of those in the Pure Abodes (suddhāvāsa) when their second consciousness is occurring, unwholesome states will cease in them there.

And yet, wholesome states did not arise for them there. For others—those belonging to the four-aggregate and five-aggregate realms—both unwholesome states will cease and wholesome states have arisen there.
For one in whom wholesome states have arisen in a certain place, will indeterminate states cease in that same place?
At the moment of the cessation of the final consciousness, wholesome states have arisen for them there,
but indeterminate states will not cease for them there. For others— namely, those belonging to the four-constituent and five-constituent existences—
both wholesome states have arisen and indeterminate states will cease there.
Or conversely, for whomsoever indeterminate states (abyākata-dhamma) will cease at a certain place, have wholesome states (kusala-dhamma) arisen for them there?

For those in the second moment of consciousness among the Pure Abodes (suddhāvāsa), and for non-percipient beings (asaññasatta), indeterminate states will cease there, but wholesome states have not arisen for them there. For others belonging to the four-aggregate realm (catuvokāra)...
For those belonging to the five-aggregate realm, indeterminate states will cease there and wholesome states have arisen there.
For whomsoever unwholesome states have arisen there, will indeterminate states cease there for them?
At the moment of dissolution of the final consciousness, unwholesome states have arisen for them there, but indeterminate states do not [cease] for them there.

In that case, indeterminate states will cease. For those others belonging to the four-aggregate or five-aggregate planes, both unwholesome states have arisen and indeterminate states will cease there.
Or rather, for whomsoever indeterminate states will cease in a certain place, have unwholesome states arisen for them there?
When the second consciousness of the Pure Abodes is occurring, for those non-percipient beings, indeterminate states will cease there,

but unwholesome states have not arisen there for them. For others— those of the four-constituent and five-constituent realms— both indeterminate states will cease there and unwholesome states have arisen there.
9.2.3.6.4. Negative Person (Paccanīka-puggala) For whom wholesome states (kusala-dhammā) had not arisen, will unwholesome states (akusala-dhammā) not cease? None.
Or else, for whom unwholesome states will not cease, had wholesome states not arisen? They had arisen.
For whom wholesome states did not arise, will indeterminate states not cease for them? None.
Or rather, for whom indeterminate states will not cease, did wholesome states not arise for them? They did arise.
For whom unwholesome states did not arise, will indeterminate states not cease for them? None.
Or, for whom indeterminate states will not cease, have unwholesome states not arisen for them? They have arisen.
9.2.3.6.5. Negative Plane:
Where wholesome states have not arisen, will unwholesome states not cease there? …pe….
9.2.3.6.6. Negative Person-Space (Paccanīka-Puggalokāsa) In whom, and in what [sphere], wholesome states have not arisen, in them, and in that [sphere], will unwholesome states not cease?

In the case of those in the Pure Abodes (Suddhāvāsa) when their second consciousness is occurring, in them, and in that [sphere], wholesome states have not arisen; [but it is] not [the case that unwholesome states will not cease].
And for those [beings], unwholesome states will not cease there. For those non-percipient beings, wholesome states have not arisen there and unwholesome states will not cease there.
Or, for whomsoever unwholesome states will not cease in a certain place, have wholesome states not arisen for them there?
For those who possess the highest path (aggamagga), for Arahants, and for those whose consciousness immediately following which they will attain the highest path—
unwholesome states (akusala-dhamma) will not cease therein, yet wholesome states (kusala-dhamma) have not failed to arise therein for them.
For non-percipient beings (asaññasatta), neither unwholesome states nor wholesome states will cease therein.
And [it is such that] wholesome states have not arisen.
For whomsoever wholesome states have not arisen in a certain place, will indeterminate states cease for them there? They will cease.
Or else, for whomsoever indeterminate states will not cease in a certain place, have wholesome states arisen for them there? They have arisen.
For whom and in whatever [state] unwholesome states (*akusala-dhamma*) have not arisen, will indeterminate states (*avyākata-dhamma*) not cease there for them? They will cease.
Or rather, for whom and in whatever [state] indeterminate states will not cease, have unwholesome states not arisen there for them? They have arisen.
This concludes the section on arising and cessation.
The section on the process of existence is finished.
